Rolan is an aspiring wizard who can first be found at the Emerald Grove in Act One. He is bound for Baldur's Gate with his two siblings, where a prestigious apprenticeship awaits.
“
My Thunderwave will make quick work of any goblin - just you wait.
„
— Rolan

Involvement

Act One

Rolan is first found in the Emerald Grove arguing with  Cal and  Lia on whether they should remain in the Grove to help the tiefling refugees or leave. Rolan believes they have no allegiance or responsibility toward the refugees and should leave for Baldur's Gate for their own safety. Lia fervently argues that they should help the refugees because it is the right thing to do. She accuses him of being selfish, only caring about his apprenticeship to  Lorroakan at Baldur's Gate. The party can convince them to stay in the Grove or leave.[1]

Convince to stay

The following options convince the trio to stay:

[2]
  • [PERSUASION] You should all stay. A single blade could make a difference. (DC 10)
  • [DRAGONBORN] Clan is everything. You don't abandon those you swore to protect.
  • [TIEFLING] Have you forgotten Elturel? We should stand by our people - no one else will.
  • [BARBARIAN] Only cowards run from a fight.
  • [RANGER] I'd choose the wilderness over the dangers of a city any day. Stay.
  • [MONK] To leave is a heavy choice - it will weigh on whatever path you walk next.
  • [PALADIN] 'Where the weak have need, the strong have a duty'. Stay.

Convince to leave

The following options convince the trio to leave.

[2]
  • Get out while you can - the goblins will be back.
  • [GITHYANKI] If they cannot fight, they will die. That is as it should be.
  • [EVIL CLERIC] Why die for those who can't defend themselves?

All other options, or deciding not to interact with them causes them to leave on their own as well.

If the party convince the trio to stay, they can speak to Rolan again in the Hollow. He then explains that he has an apprenticeship under  Lorroakan. If  Gale is in the party, he asks Rolan to introduce them to Lorroakan.

If Rolan survives ⁠Defeat the Goblins, he attends the Campsite celebration and performs a magic show for Cal and Lia.

Act Two

If Rolan stays at the grove and survives Act One, he moves to the Last Light Inn where he drowns his sorrows in alcohol. He angrily tells the party that his siblings were taken to Moonrise Towers as prisoners while he was defending the children of the tiefling refugees during an attack of The Cult of the Absolute. He is angry with the party because of his perception that they are the reason his siblings were endangered and insists on going to find them himself. He then leaves to save his siblings after the party's first fast travel or long rest.

After departing, he can be found (and saved) on his rescue mission at the Ruined Battlefield, on the eastern shore of the river, south of the bridge that leads to the Reithwin Tollhouse at X: -54 Y: -111, about to be attacked by  Shadows. Saving Rolan grants the inspiration ⁠Saving the Prodigious to party members with the  Folk Hero background. If Rolan is not saved before long resting, he is afflicted by the  Shadow Curse and dies.[3]

Saving Lia and Cal before finding Rolan at the Last Light Inn results in him already being gone on his futile rescue mission by the time the party members arrive at the Inn.

Speaking to Rolan at the Inn, then saving Lia and Cal before running into him at the battlefield, might cause Rolan to die and to be afflicted by the Shadow Curse.

If Rolan was convinced to stay, but for any reason, Cal and Lia die in Act One, then Rolan will not appear at Last Light in or on the Ruined Battlefield, however he will still appear in Act Three.

If Rolan is not persuaded into staying at the Grove, he and his siblings do not appear in Act Two but a recorded message from Rolan to his siblings can be found at the Last Light Inn. His absence results in the deaths of many tiefling refugees during the Absolutist attack.

Act Three

If Rolan survives Act Two or leaves the Grove during Act One, he moves to the front desk of Sorcerous Sundries in place of  Lorroakan's Projection, although his behaviour is stiff and the narrator notes that something seems wrong.

Confronting Lorroakan

If the Nightsong goes to confront Lorroakan during ⁠Find the Nightsong, Rolan will also go up Ramazith's Tower. Whether Rolan sides with or against his master upon hearing his plans for  Dame Aylin depends on several factors:

  • If both his siblings survive Act Two, he sides automatically against Lorroakan.
  • If only one of them survives Act Two, Rolan requires either a  DC 20 Intimidation Check,  DC 18 Persuasion Check, or  DC 15 Arcana Check.
  • If neither of them are saved, he sides with Lorroakan; though he may also side with Lorroakan if his siblings were saved before the party's first visit at the Last Light Inn. This outcome also automatically happens whenever Rolan is not persuaded into staying at the grove during Act One, implying they did not survive the journey.

If Rolan dies during the confrontation,  Speak with Dead can be used to learn more of his background, including that he is not biologically related to Cal and Lia.

Lastly, if the party attack Lorroakan themselves, Rolan instead confronts the party after Lorroakan is defeated, demanding to know what happened. The talking party member must pass either a  DC 18 Persuasion Check or  DC 18 Intimidation Check or Rolan attacks.

After the battle, if Rolan sided against Lorroakan he resolves to master the tower's secrets on his own and pledges its resources to aid in the final battle, cursing Lorroakan as a bastard and confessing to suffering daily abuse from the man. After a long rest, Rolan then becomes an ally for ⁠Gather Your Allies, and levels up to Level 12.

In addition, his spells change:

  •  Colour Spray →  Rolan's Colour Spray
  •  Mage Armour →  Rolan's Mage Armour
  •  Magic Missile →  Rolan's Magic Missile
  •  Thunderwave →  Rolan's Thunderwave

Idle banter

Lia, Cal, and Rolan argue about whether to stay in the Grove during Act One:

  • Rolan
    We don't even know these people!
  • Lia
    That doesn't matter.
  • Rolan
    Of course it does. You would choose strangers over us!
  • Lia
    That's not what I said.
  • Cal
    Can we stop shouting? No?
  • Cal
    Calm down! Please.
  • Lia
    I won't leave them behind!
  • Rolan
    You're going to get us killed!

If Cal, Lia, and Rolan stay in the Grove:

  • Cal
    Don't be grumpy, Rolan. We'll get to the city soon.
  • Rolan
    I am not grumpy.
  • Cal
    The scowl on your face would frighten a troll.
  • Rolan
    Heh. You're an idiot.
  • Cal
    How long until Rolan shows off his Thunderwave?
  • Lia
    Depends. How many people are dumb enough to ask?
  • Cal
    Hah! True.

If Cal, Lia, and Rolan do not stay in the Grove:

  • Cal
    How long will it take to get to Baldur's Gate?
  • Rolan
    Depends. How often are you going to ask that?
  • Cal
    Hey, sis. How long will it take to get to Baldur's Gate?
  • Lia
    *Sigh.*
  • Rolan
    We should add the Elfsong Tavern to the list.
  • Lia
    So long as you're paying.
  • Cal
    Drinks on Rolan? Count me in.
  • Rolan
    I swear, I've never met such a pair of cheapskates.

Speak with Dead

Rolan can be spoken to with  Speak with Dead.

  • What's your name?
    • Rolan
      Rolan. Just... Rolan.
  • Do you have any family?
    • Rolan
      No... family... no one.
      • No family? What about Lia and Cal?
        • Rolan
          They are... brother and sister. Cal says... I am family, but...
  • Did you come here alone?
    • Rolan
      With Lia... and Cal. They are brother and sister. But I am... not blood.
  • How did you die?
    • Rolan
      Too fast but... can't be. Must finish...
      • Finish what?
        • Rolan
          My... training... must get to... Lorroakan.
          • What is so important about Lorroakan?
            • Rolan
              Everything. He'll make me... greatest wizard... in Faerûn.
  • Where are you from?
    • Rolan
      The city that... survived Hell.
  • Where were you going?
    • Rolan
      To Baldur's Gate... to Lorroakan... my destiny.
      • What is so important about Lorroakan?
        • Rolan
          Everything. He'll make me... greatest wizard... in Faerûn.
